meta.name: <PROJECT_NAME> Connected On-Premises Deployment Specification
meta.author: Generic Enterprise Standard
meta.description: Standard architectural requirements, packaging bundles, security constraints, and operational workflows for deploying enterprise applications in internet-connected on-premises environments.

core_principles: Zero-Knowledge / Least Privilege: The application server must operate with the minimum required privileges and avoid handling unencrypted sensitive material whenever possible.
Connected Autonomy: The application operates on-premises but leverages outbound internet access for automated updates, telemetry, and online license verification.
Portability: Single-command deployment using container orchestration (e.g., Docker Compose or Kubernetes) across standard enterprise Linux distributions.
Immutable Infrastructure: No raw source code shipped to production hosts. Only compiled binaries, container images, or minified assets are distributed.
Comprehensive Auditability: All security-relevant actions, access attempts, and state changes must be recorded in an immutable log suitable for SIEM integration.

contents: Container images (pulled directly from private registry)
bundles.installation_method: Clone repo/manifests, configure .env with online license token, run docker compose pull && docker compose up -d

contents: Compiled executable, MSI, or macOS DMG
Centralized configuration file pointing to on-prem server endpoint
bundles.installation_method: Distribute via MDM (Intune/Jamf) or manual install, launch application

minimum.network: 1 Gbps local NIC, Outbound HTTPS Access

recommended.network: 10 Gbps redundant NIC, Outbound HTTPS Access

standard_tier.engine: Embedded Database (e.g., SQLite via Docker Volume)

enterprise_ha_tier.network_restriction: localhost or internal-subnet only, TLS required

networking_and_firewall.airgap_compliance: Internet-connected deployment. Requires outbound HTTPS access to specific vendor endpoints for updates and telemetry.

encryption_model.data_in_transit: TLS 1.3 / HTTPS strictly enforced on all exposed ports.
encryption_model.data_at_rest: AES-256-GCM encryption for persistent volumes or sensitive DB rows.
encryption_model.key_management: Master keys derived securely; asymmetric public keys residing on the server, private keys residing offline.

authentication_and_authorization.mfa: Mandatory TOTP (RFC 6238) or enterprise SAML/SSO integration.
authentication_and_authorization.first_boot_bootstrap: Initial superadmin credentials printed to secure console log on first execution.
authentication_and_authorization.rbac: Strict Role-Based Access Control enforcing Separation of Duties.

governance_and_audit.approval_model: Multi-admin quorum (e.g., 2-of-3 Admins required) for destructive actions.
governance_and_audit.audit_logs: 90-day minimum retention period with syslog/JSON output for SIEM integration.

steps: 1. Authenticate to the private repository or container registry on the target server.
2. Clone the deployment repository or fetch the Docker Compose manifests.
3. Configure environment variables (.env), online license token, and TLS certificates.
4. Execute deployment command (e.g., sudo docker compose up -d).
5. Retrieve initial bootstrap admin credentials from secure console logs.
1. Pull the latest changes from the deployment branch or fetch new container tags.
2. Rebuild or restart containers (sudo docker compose pull && sudo docker compose up -d).

backup_and_recovery: Backup: Snapshot database volumes or execute native DB dumps (e.g., pg_dump).
Restore: Offline verification of backup integrity via disaster recovery scripts.

compliance_checklist: No raw source code present on deployed hosts.
Outbound internet access restricted to required vendor endpoints (updates/licensing) only.
All secrets/keys excluded from version control and bundles.
TLS enabled on all exposed ports.
Audit logging enabled and retention period documented.
